profile_headline: DATAcated® to telling stories with data | Runner | Mom of 2 | LinkedIn Top Voice in Data Science & Analytics | Learning to Play Guitar
post_content:
One of my first views into the world of programming a computer to do your work
for you was about 10 years ago. I was working for a bank that was required to
provide a full list of their high-risk third-party-vendors. We requested the
data on all vendors that the bank had used over the year. In return, we were
sent a 20 inch stack of printed papers in a box that listed out every
transaction with a vendor that the bank has had in the past year. My task was
to look through every single line item (by hand) and determine if the amount
of the transaction was higher than our threshold and then type in the vendor
name in a spreadsheet and assign a risk rating (based on our methodology)... I
started plugging away, I knew it would take WEEKS to get through this task. I
was dreading it because it was so repetative and prone to error. On day 2 of
my effort, the head of operational risk walked by my desk and asked what I was
doing with all this paper... when I explained the request, he laughed and said
he had a 'better solution'. After he called the person that owned the data and
requested access (which took about 20 minutes). He wrote a program that did
everything I needed to do in about 10 minutes!!! I was so inspired and still
remember this day clearly! hashtag#programming hashtag#data
